0.title: He Must Increase, I Must Decrease
0.overview:
Pride is the sin we see most easily in others and least easily in ourselves. It is often called the root of all other sins, because at its heart it is the desire to be our own god. Humility, by contrast, is one of the most attractive qualities a person can have, and one of the hardest to pursue, because the moment we think we have it, we have lost it.

Scripture speaks of pride and humility again and again. God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble (Jas 4:6; 1 Pet 5:5). That one sentence explains why humility matters so much. Grace flows downhill, to the low places. The proud shut themselves off from the very grace they need.

This study looks at what pride is, how Christ shows us true humility, why God opposes the proud, what humility looks like in everyday life and how we can grow in it. John the Baptist summed up the goal: He must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30).

Five units: (1) Pride: The Root Sin; (2) The Humility of Christ; (3) God Opposes the Proud; (4) What Humility Looks Like; (5) Growing in Humility.

1.title: Pride: The Root Sin
1.overview:
Pride at the beginning. The serpent's temptation in Eden appealed to pride: you will be like God, knowing good and evil (Gen 3:5). Adam and Eve were not content to be creatures. They wanted to decide for themselves what was good. Every sin since has carried the same seed: putting ourselves in God's place.

What pride is. Pride is an inflated view of ourselves and a deflated view of God. It shows itself in many ways: boasting, self-righteousness, a critical spirit, an unteachable heart, a need for praise, resentment when overlooked, refusal to admit wrong and contempt for others. It can even hide behind false humility, in people who talk constantly about their own failures so that others will reassure them.

Pride is deceptive. The pride of your heart has deceived you (Obad 3). Edom felt secure in its rocky heights, but God said, Though you soar aloft like the eagle, though your nest is set among the stars, from there I will bring you down (Obad 4). Pride blinds us to our weakness and our danger.

Pride goes before a fall. Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall (Prov 16:18). King Nebuchadnezzar walked on his palace roof and said, Is not this great Babylon, which I have built by my mighty power as a royal residence and for the glory of my majesty? (Dan 4:30). That very hour he was humbled, driven from people and made to live like an animal, until he acknowledged that the Most High rules the kingdom of men (Dan 4:32).

God hates pride. Among the things the LORD hates, the first listed is haughty eyes (Prov 6:17). Pride and arrogance and the way of evil and perverted speech I hate (Prov 8:13). Pride is not a small fault. It is a direct challenge to God's glory.
1.theology:
Pride and self-esteem: Modern culture often treats low self-esteem as the main human problem. Scripture says our deeper problem is that we think too much of ourselves and too little of God. Humility is not thinking badly of ourselves but thinking rightly, and thinking of ourselves less.

Proper pride? Paul can speak of boasting in the Lord (1 Cor 1:31), of being proud of other believers' faith (2 Cor 7:4), and of a craftsman's satisfaction in good work. These are not sinful pride. Sinful pride takes credit for what God has given and lifts us above others.

Spiritual pride: The most dangerous pride is religious: pride in our knowledge, our gifts, our morality or our doctrinal correctness. Jesus' harshest words were for the proud religious leaders of his day.
1.examples:
Then: King Uzziah was greatly blessed by God and became powerful. But when he was strong, he grew proud, to his destruction (2 Chr 26:16). He entered the temple to burn incense, a task reserved for priests, and was struck with leprosy. Success is often more dangerous to the soul than failure.

Now: A capable church leader is praised often for his preaching. Slowly he begins to resent anyone who questions him and to speak dismissively of other churches. A friend lovingly points this out. At first he is defensive. Then he sees it, confesses his pride and asks for prayer. His ministry becomes gentler and more fruitful.

A simple test: How do you react when you are corrected, overlooked or criticised? Your reaction reveals the level of your pride.

verseByVerse.quote: Now the serpent was more crafty than any other beast of the field that the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, "Did God actually say, 'You shall not eat of any tree in the garden'?" And the woman said to the serpent, "We may eat of the fruit of the trees in the garden, but God said, 'You shall not eat of the fruit of the tree that is in the midst of the garden, neither shall you touch it, lest you die.'" But the serpent said to the woman, "You will not surely die. For God knows that when you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil." So when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took of its fruit and ate, and she also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The serpent's promise was that they would be like God. That was the hook. Pride does not usually present itself as rebellion. It presents itself as wisdom, freedom or self-fulfilment. But at its root, it is the desire to be our own authority, refusing the place God has given us.

verseByVerse.quote: All this came upon King Nebuchadnezzar. At the end of twelve months he was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon, and the king answered and said, "Is not this great Babylon, which I have built by my mighty power as a royal residence and for the glory of my majesty?" While the words were still in the king's mouth, there fell a voice from heaven, "O King Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: The kingdom has departed from you, and you shall be driven from among men, and your dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field. And you shall be made to eat grass like an ox, and seven periods of time shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules the kingdom of men and gives it to whom he will." Immediately the word was fulfilled against Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from among men and ate grass like an ox, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven till his hair grew as long as eagles' feathers, and his nails were like birds' claws. At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my reason returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and praised and honored him who lives forever, for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom endures from generation to generation; all the inhabitants of the earth are accounted as nothing, and he does according to his will among the host of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth; and none can stay his hand or say to him, "What have you done?" At the same time my reason returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom, my majesty and splendor returned to me. My counselors and my lords sought me, and I was established in my kingdom, and still more greatness was added to me. Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honor the King of heaven, for all his works are right and his ways are just; and those who walk in pride he is able to humble. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Nebuchadnezzar's boast was barely out of his mouth when God's judgment fell. He lost his reason and lived like an animal until he lifted his eyes to heaven. Then his reason returned and he praised the King of heaven, saying that those who walk in pride he is able to humble. The proudest king on earth learned humility the hard way.

verseByVerse.quote: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock, in your lofty dwelling, who say in your heart, "Who will bring me down to the ground?" Though you soar aloft like the eagle, though your nest is set among the stars, from there I will bring you down, declares the LORD. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Edom lived in rocky strongholds and felt untouchable. God says their pride has deceived them. No height is high enough to escape God. Pride makes us feel secure precisely when we are most in danger.

verseByVerse.quote: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall. It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor than to divide the spoil with the proud. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Pride comes before destruction. And Proverbs adds a striking comparison: it is better to be lowly with the poor than to share the spoil with the proud. Humility with poverty is better than pride with wealth. God's values turn the world's upside down.

1.reflection:
In what forms does pride most often show itself in your life?

Why is pride so hard to see in ourselves?

Read Daniel 4. What did Nebuchadnezzar learn, and how?

Is there an area of success in your life that could become a source of pride?

2.title: The Humility of Christ
2.overview:
The greatest example of humility is not a saint or a monk but the Son of God himself.

He emptied himself. Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, by taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men. And being found in human form, he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross (Phil 2:5-8). The one who had every right to glory chose the lowest place. Humility is not weakness. It is strength choosing to serve.

He washed feet. On the night before his death, Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, rose from supper, took a towel and washed his disciples' feet, the task of the lowest servant (John 13:3-5). His humility flowed from security, not insecurity. He knew who he was, so he did not need to prove it. Then he said, For I have given you an example, that you also should do just as I have done to you (John 13:15).

He was gentle and lowly. Jesus described himself in these terms: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls (Matt 11:29). The Lord of the universe is approachable. He did not lord it over people. He welcomed children, ate with sinners and touched lepers.

He came to serve. For even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many (Mark 10:45). His greatness was shown in service.

He was exalted. Because Christ humbled himself, God has highly exalted him (Phil 2:9). The path to glory ran through humility. This is the pattern for his followers too.
2.theology:
Humility is Godlike: We might think humility is only for creatures, but Christ's humility reveals something about God himself. The Son delights to serve the Father's purpose, and God stoops to dwell with the lowly (Isa 57:15). Humility is part of the beauty of God's character.

Humility is learned in union with Christ: Paul says Have this mind because it is yours in Christ Jesus. We do not produce humility by imitation alone. We grow in it as Christ lives in us by his Spirit.

Security and service: Jesus washed feet because he knew who he was. Believers who are secure in God's love are free to serve without needing recognition.
2.examples:
Then: When James and John asked for the best seats in the kingdom, the other disciples were angry, probably because they wanted the same seats. Jesus called them together and said that among his followers, greatness means service (Mark 10:35-45). He was on his way to the cross even as they argued about thrones.

Now: A successful businesswoman volunteers at her church's community meal. She is assigned to wash dishes in the back kitchen, where no one sees her. At first she is irritated. Then she remembers John 13 and finds joy in the hidden work. It becomes the highlight of her week.

A simple test: Are you willing to do tasks that no one will see or thank you for?

verseByVerse.quote: Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility count others more significant than yourselves. Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others. Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, by taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men. And being found in human form, he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. Therefore God has highly exalted him and bestowed on him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul's command is practical: count others more significant than yourselves; look to their interests. Then he gives the reason, the greatest example of humility ever seen: the Son of God made himself nothing. And the outcome: God exalted him above every name. Humility now, glory later.

verseByVerse.quote: Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going back to God, rose from supper. He laid aside his outer garments, and taking a towel, tied it around his waist. Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet and to wipe them with the towel that was wrapped around him. He came to Simon Peter, who said to him, "Lord, do you wash my feet?" Jesus answered him, "What I am doing you do not understand now, but afterward you will understand." Peter said to him, "You shall never wash my feet." Jesus answered him, "If I do not wash you, you have no share with me." Simon Peter said to him, "Lord, not my feet only but also my hands and my head!" Jesus said to him, "The one who has bathed does not need to wash, except for his feet, but is completely clean. And you are clean, but not every one of you." For he knew who was to betray him; that was why he said, "Not all of you are clean." When he had washed their feet and put on his outer garments and resumed his place, he said to them, "Do you understand what I have done to you? You call me Teacher and Lord, and you are right, for so I am. If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have given you an example, that you also should do just as I have done to you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: John notes what Jesus knew before he took the towel: all things were in his hands, he had come from God and was going to God. Supreme security led to supreme service. Peter protested, but Jesus insisted. Then he told them to follow his example. Christian leadership is foot-washing leadership.

verseByVerse.quote: Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus invites the weary to come to him. Why should they? Because he is gentle and lowly in heart. He is not a harsh master. His yoke is easy and his burden light. The humility of Christ is not only our example; it is our comfort. He welcomes the weak.

verseByVerse.quote: And Jesus called them to him and said to them, "You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. But it shall not be so among you. But whoever would be great among you must be your servant, and whoever would be first among you must be slave of all. For even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus contrasts the rulers of the Gentiles, who lord it over others, with his followers. Among them, whoever would be great must be a servant, and whoever would be first must be a slave. The reason is Jesus himself, who came to serve and to give his life. Greatness in God's kingdom is measured by service.

2.reflection:
What does Philippians 2:5-8 teach about the nature of true humility?

Why did Jesus' security enable him to wash his disciples' feet?

How does Jesus' description of himself as "gentle and lowly" change how you approach him?

What is one hidden act of service you could do this week?

3.title: God Opposes the Proud
3.overview:
But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble." (Jas 4:6). This proverb, quoted by both James and Peter from Proverbs 3:34, is one of the most sobering statements in Scripture. God actively resists the proud. He sets himself against them. But to the humble he gives grace, and more grace.

The Pharisee and the tax collector. Jesus told a parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and treated others with contempt (Luke 18:9). A Pharisee prayed, thanking God that he was not like other men, and listing his religious achievements. A tax collector stood far off, beat his breast and prayed, God, be merciful to me, a sinner! Jesus said that the tax collector went home justified, not the Pharisee. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted (Luke 18:13-14).

Humility and salvation. Pride is the great barrier to salvation. The proud do not think they need a Saviour. Only those who see their sin and helplessness will turn to Christ. Jesus said, Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven (Matt 5:3). The kingdom belongs to spiritual beggars.

Humility and prayer. But this is the one to whom I will look: he who is humble and contrite in spirit and trembles at my word (Isa 66:2). God draws near to the humble. Proud prayers bounce off the ceiling; humble cries reach God's heart.

Humble yourselves. Both James and Peter follow the proverb with a command: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you (Jas 4:10). Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God so that at the proper time he may exalt you, casting all your anxieties on him, because he cares for you (1 Pet 5:6-7). Humility is something we choose, and God promises to lift up those who do.
3.theology:
Grace and humility: The Reformed doctrines of grace are deeply humbling. If salvation is entirely God's work, then no one can boast (Eph 2:8-9). What do you have that you did not receive? If then you received it, why do you boast as if you did not receive it? (1 Cor 4:7). Grace kills pride at the root.

Humility and anxiety: Peter links humility with casting our anxieties on God (1 Pet 5:6-7). Anxiety often comes from trying to control what only God controls. Humility accepts our limits and trusts God's care.

The exaltation of the humble: God's promise to exalt the humble may be fulfilled in this life, but it will certainly be fulfilled in the next. Mary sang, he has brought down the mighty from their thrones and exalted those of humble estate (Luke 1:52).
3.examples:
Then: Naaman, commander of the Syrian army, came to Elisha to be healed of leprosy. When told to wash seven times in the Jordan, he was furious; he had expected something grander. His servants persuaded him to obey. When he humbled himself and went down into the river, his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child (2 Kgs 5:14).

Now: A man has been coming to church for years, proud of his good life and charitable giving. One Sunday, hearing Luke 18 preached, he realises he has been praying like the Pharisee. For the first time, he prays the tax collector's prayer and means it. He later says that was the day he became a Christian.

A simple test: When you pray, do you come more like the Pharisee or the tax collector?

verseByVerse.quote: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble." Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded. Be wretched and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom. Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: James quotes the proverb and then gives a series of commands: submit to God, resist the devil, draw near to God, cleanse your hands, purify your hearts, mourn and weep over sin, humble yourselves. The promise frames it all: God gives more grace, and he will exalt the humble.

verseByVerse.quote: He also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and treated others with contempt: "Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector. The Pharisee, standing by himself, prayed thus: 'God, I thank you that I am not like other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector. I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I get.' But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, 'God, be merciful to me, a sinner!' I tell you, this man went down to his house justified, rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Pharisee's prayer is all about himself: what he is not, what he does. The tax collector's prayer is all about God's mercy. He does not compare himself with anyone. Jesus' verdict is shocking to his hearers: the tax collector, not the Pharisee, went home justified. Humility, not performance, receives God's grace.

verseByVerse.quote: Likewise, you who are younger, be subject to the elders. Clothe yourselves, all of you, with humility toward one another, for "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble." Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God so that at the proper time he may exalt you, casting all your anxieties on him, because he cares for you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter tells everyone to clothe themselves with humility toward one another. The image suggests a servant tying on an apron. God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble. So humble yourselves under his mighty hand, and cast your anxieties on him. Humility is not only an attitude to others; it is trust in God.

verseByVerse.quote: Thus says the LORD: "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool; what is the house that you would build for me, and what is the place of my rest? All these things my hand has made, and so all these things came to be, declares the LORD. But this is the one to whom I will look: he who is humble and contrite in spirit and trembles at my word. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God says heaven is his throne and earth his footstool. No temple could contain him. Yet the God who fills the universe looks with favour on one kind of person: the humble and contrite, who trembles at his word. Greatness does not impress God; humility does.

3.reflection:
What does it mean that God "opposes" the proud?

Read Luke 18:9-14. Which character are you more like?

How do the doctrines of grace humble us?

What anxieties do you need to cast on God as an act of humility?

4.title: What Humility Looks Like
4.overview:
Humility is not a feeling but a way of life. Scripture shows what it looks like in practice.

Thinking rightly about ourselves. For by the grace given to me I say to everyone among you not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think with sober judgment (Rom 12:3). Humility is not denying our gifts but seeing them accurately, as gifts from God to be used for others.

Putting others first. Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility count others more significant than yourselves. Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others (Phil 2:3-4). Humility notices others' needs and puts them ahead of our own convenience.

Being teachable. Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is stupid (Prov 12:1). A humble person can receive correction and learn from anyone, including those younger, less educated or less experienced.

Admitting wrong. Humble people say "I was wrong" and "Please forgive me" without excuses. Proud people defend, blame and justify.

Not seeking praise. Let another praise you, and not your own mouth (Prov 27:2). Jesus warned against practising righteousness to be seen by others (Matt 6:1). Humble people are content to be overlooked.

Associating with the lowly. Live in harmony with one another. Do not be haughty, but associate with the lowly. Never be wise in your own sight (Rom 12:16). Humility does not seek out only the important or impressive. It is at home with anyone.

Rejoicing in others' success. Humble people can celebrate when others are honoured, even rivals. John the Baptist, when his disciples complained that everyone was going to Jesus, said, Therefore this joy of mine is now complete. He must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:29-30).
4.theology:
Humility and confidence: Humility is not timidity. Paul was humble and bold. Moses was very meek, more than all people who were on the face of the earth (Num 12:3), yet he confronted Pharaoh. Humility rests confidence on God, not self.

Humility in leadership: Leaders are especially tempted to pride. Scripture warns that a recent convert should not be an elder, or he may become puffed up with conceit (1 Tim 3:6). Humble leaders listen, share credit, admit mistakes and serve.

Humility in disagreement: Humble Christians can hold firm convictions while recognising that they might be wrong on secondary matters, listening carefully to others and speaking gently.
4.examples:
Then: John the Baptist was the most famous prophet of his day, with crowds coming from all over Judea. Yet when Jesus appeared, John pointed his own disciples to him: Behold, the Lamb of God (John 1:36). Two of them left John and followed Jesus. John rejoiced. He knew his role was to point away from himself.

Now: A senior pastor notices that a younger assistant's preaching is better received than his own. He feels a stab of jealousy. Then he confesses it to God and decides to give the young man more opportunities to preach. He tells the church, "God has given us a gift in this brother." The young man never forgets it.

A simple test: When someone else is praised for something you are good at, what do you feel?

verseByVerse.quote: For by the grace given to me I say to everyone among you not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think with sober judgment, each according to the measure of faith that God has assigned. For as in one body we have many members, and the members do not all have the same function, so we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another. Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us, let us use them: if prophecy, in proportion to our faith; if service, in our serving; the one who teaches, in his teaching; the one who exhorts, in his exhortation; the one who contributes, in generosity; the one who leads, with zeal; the one who does acts of mercy, with cheerfulness. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul tells believers not to think too highly of themselves, but to think soberly. Then he explains why: we are all members of one body, each with different gifts. No member is self-sufficient. Humility recognises both our gifts and our need of others.

verseByVerse.quote: I have applied all these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, brothers, that you may learn by us not to go beyond what is written, that none of you may be puffed up in favor of one against another. For who sees anything different in you? What do you have that you did not receive? If then you received it, why do you boast as if you did not receive it? (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Corinthians were puffed up, taking sides with different leaders. Paul asks three questions. Who sees anything different in you? What do you have that you did not receive? If you received it, why boast? Every gift, talent and advantage we have is a gift. There is nothing left to boast about.

verseByVerse.quote: And they came to John and said to him, "Rabbi, he who was with you across the Jordan, to whom you bore witness—look, he is baptizing, and all are going to him." John answered, "A person cannot receive even one thing unless it is given him from heaven. You yourselves bear me witness, that I said, 'I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before him.' The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. Therefore this joy of mine is now complete. He must increase, but I must decrease." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: John's disciples were worried that Jesus was becoming more popular. John answered that he was only the friend of the bridegroom, and his joy was complete. He must increase, but I must decrease. These words are a motto for every Christian. Our joy is in seeing Christ honoured, not ourselves.

verseByVerse.quote: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring. Let another praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Two short warnings: do not boast about tomorrow, because you do not know what it will bring; and let others praise you, not your own mouth. Humility is honest about our limits and leaves our reputation in God's hands.

4.reflection:
Which mark of humility in this unit is weakest in your life?

How do you respond to correction? Think of a recent example.

Read 1 Corinthians 4:7. What gifts are you tempted to boast about as if you earned them?

Whose success can you celebrate this week, even if it is hard?

5.title: Growing in Humility
5.overview:
No one becomes humble by trying to feel humble. Humility grows as we see God and ourselves rightly. Scripture shows several ways.

Look at God. When Isaiah saw the Lord, he said, Woe is me! (Isa 6:5). When Job heard God speak from the whirlwind, he said, I despise myself, and repent in dust and ashes (Job 42:6). Nothing humbles us like a true sight of God's greatness and holiness. When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have set in place, what is man that you are mindful of him? (Ps 8:3-4).

Look at the cross. The cross shows how serious our sin is: it took the death of God's Son to forgive it. And it shows how great God's love is. No one can stand at the cross and feel proud.

Accept God's humbling. God often humbles his children through weakness, failure, illness or disappointment. Paul said a thorn was given me in the flesh to keep him from becoming conceited. He asked three times for it to be removed. God answered, My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness (2 Cor 12:7-9). Paul learned to boast in his weaknesses. Hard providences, received rightly, are schools of humility.

Choose the lower place. Jesus told guests at a feast not to take the place of honour but the lowest place, so that the host might invite them up (Luke 14:7-11). Humility can be practised: choosing to serve, to listen, to give way, to take the less noticed role.

Quieten your soul. O LORD, my heart is not lifted up; my eyes are not raised too high; I do not occupy myself with things too great and too marvelous for me. But I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother (Ps 131:1-2). Humility brings rest. The proud are restless, always striving to prove themselves. The humble rest in God.

Pray for humility. Humility is a grace from God. Ask him for it, honestly, knowing that he may answer through humbling circumstances.
5.theology:
Humility and joy: Pride makes people miserable, always comparing, never satisfied. Humility frees us to enjoy God, others and life without the burden of self-promotion.

Humility is never finished: Even mature Christians struggle with pride. The fight continues until glory. But God is patient, and he finishes what he starts.

Self-forgetfulness: The goal is not constant self-examination for signs of pride, which can itself become self-focused. The goal is to be so taken up with Christ and with others that we think about ourselves less.
5.examples:
Then: In letters written over several years, Paul called himself the least of the apostles (1 Cor 15:9), then the very least of all the saints (Eph 3:8), and finally the foremost of sinners (1 Tim 1:15). Growing in Christ did not make him think more of himself, but less.

Now: A man who prided himself on his independence suffers a stroke and must depend on others for everything. At first he is bitter. Slowly, as his church family cares for him, he learns to receive help with gratitude. He tells his pastor, "I think God had to take away my strength to teach me humility. I'm grateful, though I wouldn't have chosen it."

A simple test: When did you last spend time simply looking at God's greatness, in creation or in Scripture, until you felt small?

verseByVerse.quote: O LORD, my heart is not lifted up; my eyes are not raised too high; I do not occupy myself with things too great and too marvelous for me. But I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; like a weaned child is my soul within me. O Israel, hope in the LORD from this time forth and forevermore. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This short psalm is a picture of humble contentment. David does not reach for things too great for him. He has calmed his soul like a weaned child, no longer demanding but simply resting with its mother. And he calls Israel to hope in the LORD. Humility and hope go together.

verseByVerse.quote: So to keep me from becoming conceited because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations, a thorn was given me in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to harass me, to keep me from becoming conceited. Three times I pleaded with the Lord about this, that it should leave me. But he said to me, "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me. For the sake of Christ, then, I am content with weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and calamities. For when I am weak, then I am strong. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul's thorn was given to keep him from pride after extraordinary revelations. He prayed for its removal, but God gave him grace instead. Paul learned that God's power is made perfect in weakness. So he would boast in his weaknesses, because when he was weak, he was strong.

verseByVerse.quote: Now he told a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the places of honor, saying to them, "When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not sit down in a place of honor, lest someone more distinguished than you be invited by him, and he who invited you both will come and say to you, 'Give your place to this person,' and then you will begin with shame to take the lowest place. But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when your host comes he may say to you, 'Friend, move up higher.' Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at table with you. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus watched guests scramble for the best seats at a dinner. He told them to take the lowest place instead. Better to be invited up than sent down. Then the principle: everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted. God is the host, and he decides who sits where.

verseByVerse.quote: When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have set in place, what is man that you are mindful of him, and the son of man that you care for him? Yet you have made him a little lower than the heavenly beings and crowned him with glory and honor. You have given him dominion over the works of your hands; you have put all things under his feet, all sheep and oxen, and also the beasts of the field, the birds of the heavens, and the fish of the sea, whatever passes along the paths of the seas. O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: David looks at the night sky and wonders why God would care for human beings. Yet God has crowned humanity with glory and honour and given them dominion. Humility and dignity belong together. We are small, but loved. And the psalm begins and ends with God's majestic name, not ours.

5.reflection:
How has seeing God's greatness humbled you?

Has God used weakness or failure to humble you? What did you learn?

What is one way you could "take the lower place" this week?

Read Psalm 131 slowly and pray it as your own.
